leadIn.title: Lead-In & Context: Articles: A / An / The
leadIn.content: I saw a dog in the park. The dog was playing with a ball. Notice when we introduce something new versus when we know which specific one.

meaningCheck.question: Function check: What is the primary purpose of using Articles: A / An / The?
options: To express clear, level-appropriate meaning in structured context
To translate sentences word-for-word from another language
It is an obsolete form never used by native speakers
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · This structure provides explicit grammatical function and clarity.

meaningCheck.question: Form check: Does correct usage of Articles: A / An / The require matching subject, verb, and modifier agreements?
options: No, agreement rules are optional in English
Yes, matching grammatical forms ensures natural, accurate communication
Agreement only matters in formal academic writing
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · Accurate form and agreement choices prevent misunderstandings.

form.title: Form & Structure: Articles: A / An / The
form.content: A + consonant sound (a book), An + vowel sound (an apple). Use 'the' for specific items known to both speaker and listener.

pronunciation.title: Pronunciation Notes: Articles: A / An / The
pronunciation.content: Spoken stress, weak forms, intonation, and articulation patterns for Articles: A / An / The.

controlledPractice.question: 'She has ___ apple.'
controlledPractice.explanation: Apple starts with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an'.

controlledPractice.question: 'I saw a dog. ___ dog was brown.'
controlledPractice.explanation: Once something is already mentioned, use 'the'.

controlledPractice.question: 'I like ___ music.' (talking about music in general)
controlledPractice.explanation: General, uncountable ideas usually take no article at all.
